exceptions.reason: The runtime services use PostgreSQL and neither open attacker-supplied SQLite databases nor expose arbitrary SQL or FTS5. Debian still lists the exact Trixie package as vulnerable with no stable fix and classifies it as a minor no-DSA issue.

The runtime services use PostgreSQL and neither open attacker-supplied SQLite databases nor expose arbitrary SQL or FTS5. Debian still lists the exact Trixie package as vulnerable with no stable fix and classifies it as a minor no-DSA issue.

The services use standard Unicode encodings and do not expose ungetwc over attacker-selected overlapping encodings. Debian still lists the exact Trixie package as vulnerable with no stable fix and classifies it as a minor no-DSA issue.
The services do not invoke scanf %mc with attacker-controlled width values. Debian still lists the exact Trixie package as vulnerable with no stable fix and classifies it as a minor no-DSA issue.

The services do not call gzprintf or gzvprintf and do not use non-blocking gzwrite with externally managed buffers. Debian lists the exact Trixie package as vulnerable with no fixed version available.

The services do not accept attacker-controlled PCRE2 patterns or call pcre2_dfa_match. Upstream confirms that applications using only trusted patterns or other match APIs are not exposed; Debian Trixie has not yet packaged the fixed PCRE2 10.48 release.
